title: The real cost and limitations of the 3CX AI Receptionist
summary: Dive into the features of the 3CX AI Receptionist. Learn what it does, what it costs, and how it compares to alternatives like Quo.
body_markdown:
3CX is a software-based business phone system. It markets itself as a contact center solution for companies with 25+ users. In July 2026, they launched their first AI Receptionist, designed to handle inbound calls, use AI transcription, automatically screen spam calls, and more.


That said, it still has performance, cost, and feature limitations that may limit its potential as a business solution.


This article explains 3CX AI Receptionist’s main features, pricing, and limitations. We’ll also recommend the best alternative if you want a flexible, highly capable virtual receptionist for your business.


##


What is the 3CX AI Receptionist?


The 3CX AI Receptionist is an AI-powered tool that lets companies create a virtual phone agent that works within the 3CX platform. It can answer incoming calls and speak to customers in real time without a human present. It can also understand natural human language and handle multiple calls at a time.


The 3CX AI Receptionist is part of the core 3CX platform. It requires the highest tier — 3CX AI Edition — which starts at $575 for up to eight simultaneous calls and 40 users max.


It isn’t available as a standalone product, so you can’t use it outside of the 3CX phone system.


##


What can the 3CX AI Receptionist do?


3CX’s AI Receptionist comes with features like:


- [Call routing](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing) **.** Your AI agent can route callers by topic or by name. Callers don’t need to wade through traditional phone menus to reach the right person or department.
- **Multiple language support.** 3CX’s Receptionist can help answer calls in multiple languages with its integration with OpenAI. At present, it can speak in[57 different languages](https://community.openai.com/t/what-languages-does-the-new-tts-api-support/485153) .


- **Answer questions.** The AI answers frequently asked questions based on information you add to your knowledge base. If it can’t help or doesn’t know how to answer a question, it uses fallback routing to transfer the call to a rep or your voicemail.
- **Call filtering.** The AI Receptionist filters out spam, abusive, or non-responsive callers. This gives your team time to focus on more productive conversations.
- **Check availability.** When 3CX’s AI Receptionist transfers a call, it first verifies whether the person is free to pick up. This helps ensure the AI sends callers to an available rep rather than a recorded message or voicemail.
- **Custom greetings.** Personalize your AI Receptionist’s welcome message. You can help give your callers better context and let them know they’re speaking with an AI voice agent.
- **Customizable persona.** Control the voice style of your AI Receptionist with different voices, accents, and languages. Your AI will sound more natural to the client base you serve.


##


How much does 3CX’s AI Receptionist cost?


To access 3CX’s AI Receptionist, you need to sign up for their AI Edition. The final price depends on the number of simultaneous calls you need. For example, the base AI Edition plan supports eight simultaneous calls, which costs $575 per year. This includes a max of 40 users and/or extension numbers. If you need more, you’ll need to upgrade.


There’s *technically* no limit to the total number of voice calls your 3CX AI Receptionist can field. Instead, it depends on:


1. How many simultaneous calls your tier can accommodate
2. How many OpenAI tokens you have available


Keep in mind that 3CX requires you to manage a separate OpenAI subscription. This could make it difficult to calculate costs and bandwidth, especially if you don’t have predictable call volumes.


Here’s a quick monthly calculation of what you’ll pay if you want to use the 3CX AI Receptionist at the lowest recommended level:


Cost per month


3CX AI Edition at eight simultaneous calls $48


OpenAI Tier 3 $100


OpenAI usage limit $1,000


Monthly total $1,148


Remember that you don’t *have* to subscribe to Tier 3 to use the 3CX Receptionist. But 3CX indicates that using a lower OpenAI Tier could risk performance issues like the AI Receptionist suddenly switching off mid-call. While not all businesses will hit the usage limit regularly, call volumes can still be hard to predict. And, depending on length, a single call can still use up a large number of tokens.


Here’s what a 3CX AI Edition subscription includes in addition to its AI Receptionist:


- Custom greetings
- Call routing
- Call transcription
- Call recordings
- Automatic language switching
- Lead capture
- AI knowledge base
- Call filtering
- OpenAI and Grok compatibility
- CRM integrations with Odoo, Zendesk, Microsoft Dynamics, Salesforce, Zoho CRM, and more


##


7 Key 3CX AI Receptionist limitations


The AI Receptionist is a new addition to the CX platform. As a result, it has several limitations that make it a challenging option for small businesses. Here are a few of them:


### 1. Bring Your Own AI


3CX advertises its AI Receptionist as “powered by OpenAI.” But what they *don’t* tell you is that you’re responsible for the account. You have to pay for the OpenAI subscription, provide the tokens, and handle billing or usage problems.


Running out of tokens can cause the AI agent to become unresponsive in the middle of a call. This can also happen to businesses with free or low-tier subscriptions to OpenAI, which often hit the company’s rate limits.


3CX’s officially recommended remedy is to pay OpenAI more money and subscribe to a higher tier. But for small and growing businesses, this can get expensive fast. You’re not only paying for 3CX’s most expensive Edition for AI access, but you also need to purchase a higher-tier OpenAI plan.


### 2. Pay for your own tokens


All AI applications use tokens, which are units of data that an AI model uses and generates. Many AI companies like OpenAI and Claude charge for token consumption, but services that incorporate AI on their platform generally factor token costs into the monthly rate they charge users.


Not 3CX, though. Unlike other business phones with AI receptionists, 3CX won’t pay for any of the tokens your AI agents use. This can become problematic since everything your AI agent does uses tokens. Also, the more complicated the AI’s task is, the more tokens it consumes.


3CX’s own calculations state that a single call can use up to 5,000 tokens between fielding a call and accessing information.


At OpenAI’s Tier 3, which 3CX recommends, users can spend up to $1,000 a month on tokens. And this is the *minimum* suggested tier.


### 3. Three-minute limit per call


3CX imposes a three-minute call limit on *all* its AI agents — including the AI Receptionist. If a call hits that three-minute limit, it’s immediately forwarded to a human or voicemail, without any transition or warning. It can be incredibly jarring to a caller and poor customer service.


Three minutes is a significant restriction for businesses that field longer calls. It’s also impractical for most industries that rely on longer calls to generate revenue. At best, three minutes is enough time to redirect a caller to another extension. But it still falls far short for anything more complicated, like an information request. For small and growing service-based businesses, it likely won’t be enough to qualify a lead and schedule an appointment.


### 4. Limited feature set


You can use the 3CX AI Receptionist to answer callers and route them to phone extensions. Beyond that, it lacks many features common to other AI agents. For example, it can’t send SMS messages during live calls. It also offers no configurable call-flow steps to control when and how the receptionist engages callers.


### 5. Fine-tuning the AI Receptionist is time-consuming


While it’s relatively simple to start using the 3CX AI Receptionist, getting it to perform the way you want is an engineer-level task. You may need to tweak multiple aspects of the AI’s functionality and behavior, such as:


- **The knowledge base.** You can’t simply upload a PDF or website to 3CX’s knowledge base and call it good. First, you need to convert files to Markdown. Then you need to remove irrelevant information so the AI won’t get confused or waste tokens searching for the right information.
- **Prompting.** Your company admin needs to write all the prompts that define the AI Receptionist’s behavior. Judging by 3CX’s multi-page instructions for AI prompting, this isn’t a simple process.
- **OpenAI configuration.** Company admins also need to configure OpenAI’s settings so that rate limits and token limits don’t stop callers from getting the best outcomes. At the same time, you don’t want to allow too many tokens per call, since it will dramatically increase your budget.


### 6. Knowledge base issues


Some past 3CX customers have had knowledge base issues where the agent pulls information from the wrong library. This happens even though they assigned one knowledge base to each department, as recommended by 3CX’s support team.


[One user](https://www.3cx.com/community/threads/ai-receptionist-not-respecting-knowledge-source.137533/) had to front-load all of the logic into the prompt, which goes against recommendations, but it was the only way to get it to work.


You should also know 3CX discourages users from uploading large CSVs into their knowledge base. That’s because the AI agent isn’t built to be a live inventory lookup engine. Doing so may result in slow, inaccurate responses and use more OpenAI tokens than necessary.


### 7. No call flow flexibility


After the initial setup, 3CX AI Receptionist always answers the phone first. That means you can’t save tokens by only using the AI Receptionist only as a fallback option.


But 3CX alternatives like Quo let you do this on every plan. You can build your own ideal call flow using a drag-and-drop interface and conditional logic. You can use Sona as an after-hours receptionist or as an option in a traditional IVR menu.


##


Other limitations of 3CX


Since 3CX AI Receptionist can only be used within its platform, you should be aware of where it falls short.


The biggest limitations of 3CX’s phone system include:


- **SIP trunk required.** 3CX requires you to purchase and install a physical SIP trunk before using the platform. This will likely require space for physical servers, LAN switches, and cabling. As you can imagine, installation can take time, which may matter if you don’t want service interruptions. A physical SIP trunk may also mean spending a lot of money on equipment you won’t need with a VoIP alternative.
- **AI is locked behind the highest Edition.** 3CX *does* have a free plan for up to 10 users, but it doesn’t include AI features. Instead, you’ll have to pay for the highest Edition to unlock AI capabilities. Then, you’ll pay extra to match the number of simultaneous calls you need.
- **Steep learning curve.** Configuration and setup can be challenging for non-technical users, especially if you’re configuring on-premises hardware and self-hosting private cloud installations.
- **Complicated pricing.** As mentioned, 3CX’s pricing depends on the number of simultaneous calls you pay for. This means you need to already know your call volume before you sign up. Otherwise, you’ll pay for more than you need.

##


**FAQs**


****Do I need 3CX to use the AI Receptionist?****


3CX AI Receptionist is part of the 3CX AI Edition and can’t be used separately. That means you’re locked into its business phone system if you want to keep using the AI Receptionist. Other 3CX alternatives offer standalone AI receptionists you can use with any VoIP system.


****Does 3CX have a free plan?****


You can sign up for 3CX’s 30-day free trial, which includes the AI Receptionist. After that, you’ll need to sign up for a paid plan.


****Is there a limit to using the 3CX AI Receptionist?****


All 3CX AI Receptionist calls are limited to three minutes. Also, keep in mind your AI usage is subject to rate limits as defined by your OpenAI subscription. This may affect your call quality or force calls to end early unless you train your 3CX AI agents to route calls to human reps quickly.
